I have farmed a long time, and at my age I do not want a complicated arrangement. I will keep the land in the crops I know well: wheat for winter, maize for summer on part of the land, and chili as my main cash crop on the better-managed part. I have good education and long experience, so I will stay disciplined with input use instead of chasing extremes. Because I have well irrigation, I will rely on timely watering rather than excessive fertilizer. For wheat, I will use improved seed, moderate nitrogen, and a few irrigations to secure a steady yield. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because it gives me better and more stable output on limited land, with moderate fertilizer and fewer pesticide sprays. For chili, since it is my main system and needs closer management, I will put the most labor, water, and crop protection there. I will use hybrid chili seed, more potassium than for the grain crops, and more irrigation and spraying because chili is more sensitive and more valuable. I will use rotary tillage for the grain stubble fields because it saves labor, but I will plough the chili ground to make a better root zone and cleaner field. I will spread my 10.1 mu across all three crops in a way that keeps income, food crop security, and labor manageable for my household of three.
